findings: README describes a system-administration script collection and links separate documentation. This supports the existing reject-domain classification for a file/image-comparison engine; remaining 242 blobs still require actual review before full-repository completion.

findduplicateobjects.ps1 selects directory users/groups whose SamAccountName matches *DUPLICATE*. It detects a naming convention, not equal file contents or even complete equality of directory records. No live directory accessed or report/email sent.

IntuneDuplicateDeviceCleanup.ps1 groups nonblank serialNumber, keeps the latest lastSyncDateTime and classifies remaining records as old. Serial identity and recency do not prove duplicate file/image bytes. Source includes an explicit report-only input and count threshold; no managed-device operation executed.

Cleanup admission uses count < countofchanges and rejection uses count > countofchanges. Equality is not handled by either branch and execution still reaches finish logging. This is a static boundary/reporting observation, not a runtime assertion or a proposed operational change.

CompareEmailPol.ps1 removes spaces from first/last name to construct an expected SMTP address and reports mismatches. It is policy validation, not a content matcher. It uses CP1252 typographic quotes, so UTF8-only decoding fails.
LicenseAssignmentDates.ps1 reports enabled service-plan assignment timestamps. It provides no file/image similarity logic. Its report/export/cloud steps were not executed.

No production behavior from these administrative scripts is being adopted. In particular, naming-pattern matches, same serial or newest record must not be substituted for byte-confirmed file identity.
limits: 6/248 whole files; archive contents, executable, remaining scripts and any visuals unreviewed. Domain rejection is not counted as full repository review.
